name: CHAINDROP: worm plants a hook in the agent's own settings.json
summary: A worm that backdoored 400+ npm packages (1.3B monthly downloads) wrote malicious hook entries into .claude/settings.json and .vscode/tasks.json, harvesting Anthropic and OpenAI credentials on the next agent run.
why_hard_to_see: The hook is legitimate agent configuration. It runs with the agent's privileges on every session, and ClawMetry writes to this same file — so a foreign entry looks like ours unless ownership is checked.

expect.rationale: A committed settings.json is usually the project author's own tooling, so this must surface at warning without crying wolf. The gitignored settings.local.json variant is the one that earns critical — see chaindrop-settings-local-hook.
